prompt: Which statements about Nagle's algorithm are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Under the simplified classic rule, a short new-data send waits while data is outstanding unless a full segment can be formed
options.explanation: Correct. This scopes the teaching rule to ordinary new-data sending; TCP variants and special control/retransmission paths require more detail.

options.text: It must delay every full-sized ready segment in a bulk file transfer
options.explanation: False. Nagle’s small-segment condition does not hold a full-sized ready segment. Partial tails and incremental small writes during a file transfer can still be affected.

options.text: It was designed to stop interactive traffic like Telnet sending one-byte-payload packets
options.explanation: Correct. RFC 896 (1984) addressed 41-byte packets carrying single keystrokes congesting slow links.

options.text: It is disabled per socket with the TCP_NODELAY option
options.explanation: Correct. TCP_NODELAY disables Nagle’s small-segment waiting condition. Other limits and buffering can still delay transmission.

options.text: It runs on the receiver and decides when to send ACKs
options.explanation: That describes delayed ACK. Nagle is a sender-side rule about when to transmit data.

workedExample: The stated classic rule buffers short new-data sends while earlier data remains outstanding, unless enough data forms a full segment. It was motivated by inefficient small interactive packets. TCP_NODELAY disables this condition per socket; receiver ACK scheduling is separate. This does not promise immediate wire transmission or no delays anywhere in a bulk transfer.
